intro:
Use it for the turns of a conversation with an assistant. `from="user"` is what the person wrote, in a bubble on the trailing side. `from="assistant"` is the answer, set as prose across the full width with no bubble, because an answer is long and is the thing being read.

`Message.BubbleContent` sets paragraphs, lists, inline code, code blocks and headings, so Markdown rendered to HTML can go straight in.

It lays turns out and does not scroll them. Put the turns in a scrolling column of your own, and the composer under it; [Prompt](/docs/web/components/prompt) is one.
usage:
<Message from="user">
  <Message.Content>
    <Message.Bubble>
      <Message.BubbleContent>How do I make it for six?</Message.BubbleContent>
    </Message.Bubble>
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

<Message from="assistant">
  <Message.Avatar>
    <Avatar alt="Assistant" shape="square" size="sm" fallback={<SparklesIcon />} />
  </Message.Avatar>
  <Message.Content>
    <Message.Bubble>
      <Message.BubbleContent>Multiply by 1.5…</Message.BubbleContent>
    </Message.Bubble>
    <Message.Actions>
      <Message.Action label="Copy" copy={answer} />
    </Message.Actions>
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

parts.Group: Turns in a row from the same side, set closer together. Its `from` applies to every `Message` in it.
parts.Avatar: Who the turn is from, beside its first line. Put an [Avatar](/docs/web/components/avatar) in it. In a group, leave it empty on the later turns so they line up.
parts.Content: The column that holds the rest. On a person's turn it is at most 80% of the width.
parts.Header: A line above the turn: a name in `<strong>`, a time.
parts.Attachments: The files sent with a turn, above its bubble.
parts.Attachment: One file. With `src` it is a picture; without, a card with an `icon`, the `name` and a `meta` line.
parts.Status: What the assistant is doing before its first word, as a line that shimmers. It is a `role="status"`, so it is read out as it changes. Swap it for the bubble when the text starts.
parts.Bubble: The surface. A person's turn is drawn in a muted bubble; an assistant's draws nothing.
parts.BubbleContent: The text, set as prose. With `streaming` on the `Message`, a caret follows the last word.
parts.Footer: A line under the turn: seen, edited, how long it took.
parts.Actions: The row of actions under an answer. `reveal="hover"` hides it until the turn is hovered or focused, for answers before the latest; on a touch screen it always shows.
parts.Action: An icon button with a tooltip. `label` is required, because the button has no text. `copy` puts its text on the clipboard and shows a check for a moment. `pressed` makes it a toggle, such as a thumbs-up.
parts.Branch: "‹ 2 / 3 ›", for stepping between versions of an answer that was retried or edited. `count`, `index` from 0, and `onIndexChange`.

examples.title: Actions and versions
examples.description: Copy, rate, retry and share, with `Message.Branch` to step between versions. Retry here adds a version and shows it. The ratings are `pressed` toggles.

examples.title: While it is being written
examples.description: `Message.Status` holds the place while the assistant works, then the text arrives with `streaming` set, which draws a caret after the last word and marks the turn busy. The actions appear when it is done.

examples.title: Attachments
examples.description: `Message.Attachments` above the bubble: a picture by `src`, and a file as a card with an icon, its name and a line of detail.

examples.title: Names, times and groups
examples.description: In a thread several people share, `Message.Header` carries the name and `Message.Footer` a status. `Message.Group` sets consecutive turns from one side closer together.

examples.title: With a composer
examples.description: A conversation that works: write in the [Prompt](/docs/web/components/prompt), and a stand-in model answers. Earlier answers keep their actions out of sight until they are hovered.

notes:
### Accessibility

A streaming turn is `aria-busy`, so a screen reader reads it once it is finished rather than a word at a time. `Message.Status` is a `role="status"`. Each action has its `label` as its accessible name, and `Message.Actions` is a toolbar named "Message actions".

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion turned on, the caret does not pulse and the status line does not shimmer.

### Rendering Markdown

`Message.BubbleContent` styles the HTML that Markdown renders to: `p`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `strong`, `a`, `code`, `pre` and `h3`. Render the Markdown with the library you already use and put the result inside it.
